falsifier.challenge: Construct P_n,T_n,S_n with S_n=P_n+T_n, T_n=O(1) (hence also under the stronger R5 superpolynomial-small premise), and fixed A>=0 such that exactly one of P_n,S_n is O(n^A).
falsifier.verification: Triangle inequality rules out the challenge: |S_n|<=|P_n|+|T_n| and |P_n|<=|S_n|+|T_n|. Since n^A>=1 for n>=1, an O(1) tail is absorbed into O(n^A) in both directions.
